This indicates that Cyclosporine may influence the expression or function of Abcc2 through its interaction with Lamivudine. The lowest common ancestor of these entities is the Organooxygen Compound, suggesting a shared biochemical pathway. The evidence implies that Cyclosporine could modulate Abcc2 activity via Lamivudine, though the exact mechanism remains unclear. The strength of the evidence is moderate, as it relies on indirect connections through intermediate entities. Further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the direct interaction between Cyclosporine and Abcc2.
